newsitem.title: USA: NYC mayor gains in fight over airport rents - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC mayor gains in fight over airport rents - paper.

text.p: New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani won a victory in a long battle with Port Authority over about $500 million in back rent he says is owed by the city's two airports, New York Times reported Thursday.

The Federal Aviation Administration partly reversed a decision it reached in November, when it said the mayor had no grounds for at least $220 million of the amount he said was owed by Kennedy International and La Guardia Airports, which are run by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey and leased from the city.
Private arbitrators are trying to settle the dispute, and the aviation agency's general counsel had said they were obliged to follow the ruling.

The city's corporation counsel sued over the issue, and in a letter to the city, the aviaition agency's general counsel, Nicholas Garaufis, said Wednesday the ruling was advisory, not binding on the arbitrators.
